column2: Or one should practice three months of Chandrayana with controlled senses. Having willingly done any act causing loss of caste,
one should do Shantapana or Krichchhra; Prajapatya if unwillingly. In acts that make mixed caste or vessel-loss, a month's Aindava purification;
in defiling acts a hot barley gruel three days. A quarter of the Brahmin-killing is remembered for killing a Kshatriya;
for a Vaishya living rightly an eighth; for a Shudra a sixteenth is to be known. Having killed a cat, mongoose, blue jay, frog,
dog, iguana, owl or crow one should perform the Shudra-killing vow. Having killed a woman of any of the four castes, unestablished,
having killed a woman unknowingly, one should perform the Shudra-killing vow. For killing snakes and the like, boneless creatures, night-time breath-control;
having stolen things of little value from another's house, one should do Shantapana or Krichchhra; the vow completed, he is cleared.
For stealing edibles and foods, vehicles, beds and seats, flowers, roots and fruits, the five cow-products purify;
of grass, wood and trees, dry food, jaggery, cloth, hides and flesh, three nights' fasting.
Of jewels, pearls, coral, copper, silver, iron, bronze and stones, twelve days eating grain-bits;
of cotton, insect-eaten things, cloven-hoofed and one-hoofed, birds, scents and herbs, and ropes, three days of milk.
One should perform the teacher's-bed vow for casting seed in one's own womb-sisters, a friend's or son's wives, and virgins and low-caste women;
having gone to father's sister's daughter, sister, sister's daughter and one's mother's own, mother's and brother's relative, one should perform Chandrayana.
A man who has cast seed in non-human females, in a menstruating woman, in non-wombs and in water, should perform Krichchhra and Shantapana.
Having engaged in intercourse, with man or woman, a twice-born should bathe with clothes on in a cow-cart, in water and by day.
Having gone to Chandalas and low-caste women, eaten and accepted from them, a Brahmin falls by ignorance; by knowledge he goes to equality.
A husband should confine in one house a wife defiled by a Brahmin; whatever vow is for a man with another's wives, she should practice.
If she is again corrupted, solicited by one of equal class, Krichchhra and Chandrayana are remembered as her purification.
Whatever a twice-born does by one night's service to a Shudra woman, eating alms and constantly repeating, he removes in three years.
A twice-born should perform Chandrayana or Taptakrichchhra, if mixed with vessels contaminated by Chandalas and the despised;
having eaten and drunk with them he is purified in six nights. Having eaten the leavings of low-caste people, the twice-born
should perform the Chandrayana vow; a Shudra three nights. One who unknowingly drinks water from a Chandala's well or vessel,
a twice-born should do Shantapana; a Shudra should fast a day. A twice-born who drinks water touched by a Chandala
should do three nights; a Shudra fast a day. If a twice-born is touched by leavings, a dog or a Shudra,
having fasted one night he is purified by the five cow-products. By Vaishya and Kshatriya a bath at night should be done.
A Brahmin on a journey in a waterless wilderness, who relieves himself carrying cooked food in hand,
without putting the thing down, having kept it on the body, having done cleansing, sprinkling the food, should show it to the sun and fire.
For those gone with barbarians or thieves, or travelers in wilderness, I shall tell their atonement for purification of edible and inedible:
having returned to their country, of the castes in order: after Krichchhra the Brahmin deserves the sacrament again;
at a quarter less, the Kshatriya; at a half the Vaishya; having done a quarter, the Shudra is purified by giving gifts.
A menstruating woman of the same caste touched by a menstruating woman, bathed the same day, attains purity without doubt.
A menstruating woman should not eat if touched by one of lower caste; until she attains purity she is purified by pure bathing.
Having urinated and walked the road, if from lapse of memory one drinks water, having fasted a day and night he is purified by the five cow-products.
A twice-born who has urinated without cleaning himself and eaten through delusion is purified by drinking barley for three nights.
Brahmins who have returned after taking renunciation or by force and those returned from fasting — their purification is declared:
one should perform three Krichchhras or Chandrayana, and one should be re-sanctified by birth-rite and other sacraments.
One whose sandal or impure thing touches the mouth: clay, cow-dung and the five cow-products purify.
Shaving, selling, wearing blue cloth and the like — for a Brahmin these are purified by three Krichchhras.
A menstruating woman touched by an outcaste or dog-cooker is pure on the fourth day; she should observe three nights.
Having touched Chandala, Shvapacha, pus, a woman in childbirth, a corpse or one who touched it, one is purified at once by bathing.
A Brahmin having touched a human bone with grease is purified by bathing; with water from the road, arka, durva, and with clay and water from low ground,
having vomited, in private, having bathed, one is purified by eating ghee. The barber after bathing; one who does Krichchhra eats in an eclipse;
eating with the outcast row, eating cow-products, bitten by a dog likewise pure; bitten by a worm, a suicide: by Krichchhra, repetition and oblation,
by oblation and the rest and repentance all sinners are purified.
This is called the Virasana; one who does Krichchhra is a sin-destroyer. With eight mouthfuls a day the ascetic's Chandrayana is remembered;
four in the morning and evening is the child's Chandrayana remembered; in any way two hundred and forty mouthfuls
one should eat in a month — that is the divine Chandrayana. Three days hot water, three days hot milk, three days hot ghee, three days air —
this is called Taptakrichchhra; with cold things, cold. Krichchhra-atikrichchhra with milk for twenty-one days;
cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curds, ghee, kusha water; one night's fast is called Krichchhra Shantapana;
repeated three times is called Mahashantapana; repeated by three days each is called Atishantapana.
Krichchhra called Paraka is twelve days of fasting; one meal repeated three days, then night meal, then unasked;
Prajapatya, having fasted at the end, a quarter is Krichchhrapada. With fruits a month, Phala-krichchhra; with bilva Shri-krichchhra;
with lotus seeds or amalaka; with flowers Pushpa-krichchhra; with leaves Patra-krichchhra; with water Toya-krichchhra;
with roots Mula-krichchhra; with curd, milk, buttermilk; a month of Vayavya-krichchhra by eating food in a handful;
with sesame for twelve nights the Agneya-krichchhra, destroyer of pain; for a fortnight a handful of parched grain, and the Brahmakurcha;
having fasted on the fourteenth, on the fifteenth thereafter one should eat the five cow-products, then haviṣya; having done so twice a month a man is freed from all sins.
Desiring prosperity, nourishment, or heaven, for destruction of sin, devoted to worship of the gods, the Krichchhra-doer is a sharer of all.

Knowingly, Hrishikesha, Pundarikaksha, Madhava — by uttering the three names may my sin go to destruction in a dream.
agnipuran:172:14	My bodily sin, Hrishikesha, Pundarikaksha, Madhava, quiet today, and the sin of my speech, Madhava.
agnipuran:172:15	Whatever sin I have done today while eating, sleeping, standing, going, waking or at rest, by body, mind or speech,
agnipuran:172:16	small or great, leading to bad wombs and hells — may all that be quieted by the chanting of Vasudeva.
agnipuran:172:17	Supreme Brahman, supreme abode, pure and supreme — when that Vishnu is chanted, may whatever sin I have perish.
agnipuran:172:18	That abode of Vishnu, without smell, touch and the like, which the wise reach and do not return from, may it quiet all that sin.
Whoever recites or hears this hymn that destroys sin is freed from sins done by body, mind and speech;
he goes from all sins and seizures to Vishnu's supreme abode. Therefore after sin is done one should recite the hymn that crushes all sin;
the atonement for floods of sin; the hymn is best for the vow-keeper. By atonements, hymn-recitations and vows sin is destroyed;
then those acts are for accomplishment, for enjoyment and liberation.
Having killed, one should drink milk for three days and perform Krichchhra and Chandrayana. A vow done in secret and in open is a revealer;
a hundred breath-controls should be done for removal of all sin. Drinks: of grapes, madhuka, date, palm, sugarcane,
of honey, tanka, madhvika, maireya (?), coconut; the others are not intoxicants; the flour-made liquor is declared chief.
Having drunk what is forbidden to the three castes one should be purified by drinking hot water; or one should eat grain-bits for a year, or oil-cake once at night;
for removal of drinking liquor, with child's tuft, matted hair, banner; having unknowingly eaten feces, urine, or what is touched by liquor,
the three twice-born castes deserve sacrament again. Having drunk water kept in a liquor vessel a vower for seven days;
having drunk a Chandala's water, a vower for six days; having drunk from a Chandala's well or vessels one should perform Shantapana;
having drunk the five cow-products after three nights, a twice-born who has drunk outcaste water; fish-bone, shell, conch, oyster, cowrie
and fresh water — he is purified by the five cow-products. Having drunk water from a corpse's well he is purified in three nights.
Having eaten the food of the lowest outcastes one should perform Chandrayana. In time of calamity in a Shudra's house one is purified by remorse;
a Brahmin eating from a Shudra's vessel, fasting, with the five cow-products; food cooked in a pan, in oil, oil, curds and barley meal
are not blamable from a Shudra; jaggery, milk, juices and the like. One who eats unbathed or fasts is purified at the day's end by repetition;
having urinated and eaten while unclean he is purified in three nights. What has hair, insects or fallen on it, touched by the foot willingly,
seen by a killer of an embryo, or touched by a menstruating woman, licked by crows and the like, touched by a dog,
food smelled by cows and the like — having eaten one should fast three days. One who eats semen, feces or urine should perform Prajapatya.
Chandrayana in the new first rite; Paraka in the monthly; in three fortnights Atikrichchhra; in six months Krichchhra;
in the yearly a quarter Krichchhra; one day in the repeated yearly; the yearly rite the day before, the repeated yearly the day after.
For eating forbidden food the atonement is fasting. Having eaten earth grass or garlic, one should perform the child's Krichchhra.
Having eaten food of the ineligible, leavings of women and Shudras, forbidden meat, one should drink milk for seven nights.
One who eats honey and meat, or corpse-impure or birth-impure food, should perform Prajapatya Krichchhra — a student, ascetic or vower.
Taking another's property unjustly is called theft; the gold-thief struck by the king with a pestle is purified.
Sleeping on the ground, wearing matted hair, eating leaves, roots and fruits, eating once a day, he is purified in twelve years.
